In addition, the wheel mount has a second working state, in which the part of the floating plate, on which the at least one roller is supported, is rotatably supported around a vertical axis, which is located behind the at least one wheel contact point with respect to the driving direction of a vehicle located in the roller dynamometer. Furthermore, actuators are assigned to the floating plate for rotating the part of the floating plate, on which the at least one roller is supported, around the corresponding axis in the first as well as in the second working state.

The present invention relates to a wheel mount for a vehicle test bench for motor vehicles having steerable wheels. The wheel mount comprises a floating plate and at least one roller supported on the floating plate and movable together with the floating plate in a horizontal plane.

According to the present invention, the wheel mount has a first operating state in which the portion of the floating plate on which the at least one roller is supported is rotatably supported about a vertical axis located ahead of the at least one wheel contact point on the at least one roller, as viewed in the driving direction of a vehicle positioned on the roller dynamometer.

In addition, the wheel mount has a second operating state in which the portion of the floating plate on which the at least one roller is supported is rotatably supported about a vertical axis located behind the at least one wheel contact point, as viewed in the driving direction of a vehicle positioned on the roller dynamometer.

Furthermore, actuators are assigned to the floating plate for rotating the portion of the floating plate on which the at least one roller is supported about the corresponding axis in both the first and second operating states.

The invention concerns a wheel support for a vehicle test stand intended for motor vehicles with steerable wheels. The wheel support includes a floating plate and at least one roller carried by the floating plate, the roller being movable together with the floating plate in a horizontal plane.

In accordance with the invention, the wheel support can operate in a first mode in which the portion of the floating plate carrying the at least one roller is mounted so as to rotate about a vertical axis positioned, relative to the driving direction of a vehicle situated on the roller dynamometer, in front of the at least one wheel contact point on the roller.

The wheel support also has a second operating mode in which the portion of the floating plate supporting the at least one roller is mounted for rotation about a vertical axis positioned, relative to the driving direction of the vehicle on the roller dynamometer, behind the at least one wheel contact point.

Additionally, actuators are associated with the floating plate and are configured to turn the portion of the floating plate that supports the at least one roller about the respective axis in both the first and the second operating modes.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a wheel mount for a vehicle test bench, in particular for testing motor vehicles having steerable wheels. Such a wheel mount is designed to receive and support a vehicle wheel during a test procedure while allowing movements that occur when the wheel is steered.

The wheel mount comprises a floating plate and at least one roller mounted or supported on the floating plate. The roller is configured to support the vehicle wheel, for example at the tire contact region. Both the floating plate and the roller supported thereon are movable in a substantially horizontal plane. This horizontal mobility allows the wheel mount to follow or simulate lateral and rotational movements of a steerable vehicle wheel during testing.

In a first working state, the portion of the floating plate that carries the roller is configured to rotate about a vertical axis positioned ahead of the wheel contact point, as viewed in the driving direction of the vehicle. In this operating condition, the wheel mount therefore enables a steering-related movement corresponding to a pivot point located in front of the tire contact region.

In a second working state, the portion of the floating plate supporting the roller is configured to rotate about a vertical axis positioned behind the wheel contact point, again with reference to the driving direction of the vehicle. This second operating condition allows the wheel mount to reproduce or accommodate a different steering geometry, in which the effective pivot point lies behind the tire contact region.

Actuators are assigned to the floating plate in order to produce and control the rotation of the roller-supporting portion of the floating plate. These actuators are arranged and configured such that, in both the first and the second working states, they can rotate the roller-supporting portion about the respective relevant vertical axis. As a result, the wheel mount can be actively adjusted to different steering or testing conditions and can accurately support the wheel during test bench operation.
outputs.L4:
A vehicle test bench wheel mount for steerable motor-vehicle wheels is designed to support and guide a vehicle wheel on a roller dynamometer while allowing the wheel to perform steering-related movements in a controlled manner. The wheel mount includes a horizontally movable floating plate on which at least one roller is arranged. During operation, the tire of the steerable wheel rests on the roller, so that the wheel can rotate as it would during road travel while the vehicle remains stationary on the test bench.

The floating plate is constructed so that the portion carrying the roller can be supported for rotation about a substantially vertical axis. This vertical rotational axis can be selectively positioned in different locations relative to the wheel contact point. In one operating state, the axis of rotation is located ahead of the wheel contact point when viewed in the driving direction. In another operating state, the axis of rotation is located behind the wheel contact point. By changing the position of this rotational support, the test bench can reproduce or accommodate different steering geometries and force conditions that occur during real vehicle operation.

Actuators are connected to the roller-supporting part of the floating plate and are configured to rotate this part in both operating states. These actuators may be controlled so as to impose a defined angular movement on the roller arrangement or to allow and regulate angular displacement resulting from steering forces generated by the wheel. As a result, the system can simulate the lateral and rotational behavior of a steerable wheel more accurately than a rigid roller support.

The arrangement is particularly useful for testing steering systems, suspension behavior, driver assistance functions, and vehicle dynamics on a roller dynamometer. Because the roller-supporting floating plate can move horizontally and rotate about selectable vertical axes, the test bench can better reproduce the kinematic behavior of a wheel traveling on a road surface. This makes it possible to evaluate steering response, tire behavior, and control-system performance under controlled laboratory conditions while maintaining flexibility for different vehicle types and test scenarios.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract describing a wheel mount for a vehicle test bench/roller dynamometer for motor vehicles with steerable wheels, including a floating plate, roller support, two working states with vertical pivot axes ahead of and behind the wheel contact point, and actuators for rotation.
counterfactuals.output: A wheel mount for a vehicle test bench or roller dynamometer for motor vehicles having steerable wheels includes a floating plate configured to support a vehicle wheel and to permit steering-related movement of the wheel during testing. A roller support carrying at least one running roller is mounted on or relative to the floating plate such that the wheel bears on the running roller at a wheel contact point. The wheel mount is configurable in two working states. In a first working state, the roller support is rotatable relative to a stationary frame about a substantially vertical pivot axis disposed ahead of the wheel contact point in a longitudinal direction of the vehicle. In a second working state, the roller support is rotatable about a substantially vertical pivot axis disposed behind the wheel contact point. One or more actuators are coupled to the floating plate and/or the roller support to selectively rotate the roller support about the respective vertical pivot axis and to switch between or control the two working states. The arrangement enables simulation and testing of steering behavior, aligning torque, and wheel guidance forces of steerable vehicle wheels on a test bench.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a “present invention relates to…” style patent summary for a wheel mount on a vehicle test bench, where a roller is mounted on a horizontally movable floating plate and can be rotated about different vertical axes depending on the operating state.
counterfactuals.output:
The present invention relates to a wheel mount for a vehicle test bench, in particular for receiving and supporting a vehicle wheel during testing of a motor vehicle. The wheel mount comprises a roller configured to contact and support the vehicle wheel, the roller being mounted on a floating plate which is movable in a substantially horizontal plane relative to a base or frame of the test bench.

According to the invention, the roller is arranged such that, depending on an operating state of the wheel mount or test bench, the roller is rotatable about different substantially vertical axes. In a first operating state, the roller may be pivotable about a first vertical axis, for example to permit alignment of the roller with the vehicle wheel or to compensate for lateral or angular wheel movement. In a second operating state, the roller may be rotatable about a second vertical axis, spaced from the first vertical axis, for example to enable a defined steering, centering, or positioning movement of the wheel mount.

The floating plate allows the roller to follow horizontal movements of the vehicle wheel while reducing undesired constraint forces acting on the vehicle. By selectively defining different vertical axes of rotation for the roller in different operating states, the wheel mount can provide both a floating or self-aligning behavior during a test operation and a controlled positioning or adjustment behavior during another operating condition, such as vehicle loading, unloading, calibration, or wheel alignment.

The invention thereby provides a wheel mount for a vehicle test bench which improves adaptability to wheel position and wheel movement, reduces mechanical stresses during testing, and enables reliable positioning of the roller relative to the vehicle wheel under different operating conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a European patent-style description paragraph for an invention concerning a roller dynamometer wheel mount for steerable vehicle wheels, specifying first and second working states with pivot axes respectively in front of and behind the wheel contact point in the driving direction.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a roller dynamometer wheel mount for receiving a steerable vehicle wheel during testing on a roller dynamometer, the wheel mount being configured to support the vehicle wheel such that the wheel can rotate about its wheel axis and can pivot about a substantially vertical pivot axis for simulating steering movements. The wheel mount is adjustable between at least a first working state and a second working state. In the first working state, the pivot axis of the wheel mount is arranged, with respect to a driving direction of the vehicle wheel on the roller dynamometer, in front of a wheel contact point at which the vehicle wheel contacts a roller of the roller dynamometer. In the second working state, the pivot axis is arranged, with respect to the driving direction, behind the wheel contact point. By selectively positioning the pivot axis in front of or behind the wheel contact point, different kinematic and force conditions of steerable vehicle wheels can be reproduced on the roller dynamometer, in particular for testing vehicle steering behaviour, tyre characteristics and/or driver assistance systems under defined operating conditions.
